subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: After current-main live Copilot cron proof, should aborted/no-output Copilot runs enter model fallback, or should OpenClaw rely on the 60-second idle-timeout path plus cron error status?
rationale: The remaining behavior is a side-effect-sensitive retry policy choice: falling back after an abort may recover message delivery, but it can also repeat work if tools or external writes already happened.

options.title: Prove first, keep fallback narrow
options.body: Run live current-main Copilot cron proof, then allow fallback only for idle-timeout failures before tool or outbound side effects are observed.

options.title: Fallback on aborted no-output results
options.body: Classify aborted/no-output Copilot results as fallback-worthy even when the original stream ended without a terminal response.

options.title: Do not expand fallback
options.body: Keep the current cron error surfacing and 60-second idle-timeout handling without adding a new aborted-result retry path.

recommendation.title: Prove first, keep fallback narrow
recommendation.body: Run live current-main Copilot cron proof, then allow fallback only for idle-timeout failures before tool or outbound side effects are observed.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest history on the Copilot Claude transport route and provider stream seams where the remaining policy would land.
